To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Janus Flex Stent is associated with low rates of stent thromboses and major adverse events in a population of patients at high risk of stent thrombus and that the duration of dual antiplatelet treatment after the Janus Flex was associated with similar outcomes in terms of stent thrombi and major adverse cardiovascular events.

the incidence of stent thromboses and other major adverse cardiac events was similar between 2 and 6 months of dual antiplatelet treatment after implantation of a polymer-free tacrolimus-eluted stent.

1) the Janus Flex DES is a safe and effective stent, 2) 6-month DAPT duration after implantation of this DES is associated with a low rate of stent thromboses and other major adverse events, and 3) further studies are needed to assess the optimal DAPT duration after the implantation of DESs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel method for detecting stent thromboses.
the role of the dual antiplatelet treatment (DAPT) in patients who undergo percutaneous coronary interventions.
the effects of the environment on the behavior of individuals and organizations, and the consequences of their behavior for other individuals and organizations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DAPT should be administered at least 6 months post DES, with the potential for shorter duration in selected cases.
the MATRIX registry supports <12 months DAPT duration post implantation of the tacrolimus-eluted, Janus Flex stents.

, based on the current data, 12 months DAPT duration post-DES implantation is reasonable, but that shorter durations of DAPT should be considered in selected patients and in the setting of selected lesions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not yet at a stage where we can safely recommend 3 month DAPT post-DES implantation.
the MATRIX registry supports a <12-month DAPT duration post Janus Flex stenting.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the Janus Flex is not a very safe stent, and that the MATRIX findings should be interpreted with great caution.
there is a need for individualized treatment.

the risk for thrombotic events in patients with DES is very low, especially in those with low risk for bleeding, and that DAPT duration can be tailored to each patient, lesion and DES type, based on a careful assessment of bleeding risk.
